content: To reset a forgotten password on AcmeCloud, go to the login page and select "Forgot password." Enter the email address associated with the account and submit the form. A password-reset link will be sent to that email address if an account exists for it. The link is valid for 60 minutes and can only be used once. If the link expires, request a new one from the login page. If no email arrives within a few minutes, check spam or junk folders before requesting another reset. Password resets cannot be completed over chat or phone without going through this email-based flow, since AcmeCloud does not store passwords in a recoverable form and support staff cannot see or reset a password directly on a customer's behalf.

An AcmeCloud account becomes temporarily locked after five consecutive failed login attempts within a 15-minute window. This is a security measure to prevent unauthorized access attempts. A locked account automatically unlocks after 30 minutes, or the account holder can unlock it immediately by completing a password reset. If an account remains locked repeatedly, or if the account holder suspects unauthorized access attempts, they should change their password and enable multi-factor authentication as soon as the account is accessible again. Support cannot manually unlock an account faster than the standard 30-minute window unless the account holder first verifies ownership through the identity verification process, since bypassing the lockout without verification would create a security risk.

To change the email address on file for an AcmeCloud account, the account holder must be logged in and navigate to Account Settings > Profile > Email Address. After entering the new email address, a verification link is sent to that new address, and the change only takes effect once the link is clicked. The original email address remains active and usable for login until the new one is verified. If the account holder no longer has access to the current email and cannot log in, the email change cannot be completed through self-service; this requires contacting support with identity verification, since email changes affect account recovery and are treated as a security-sensitive action.

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) can be enabled on an AcmeCloud account from Account Settings > Security > Two-Factor Authentication. Supported methods are an authenticator app using time-based one-time codes (TOTP), such as Google Authenticator or Authy, and SMS-based codes sent to a verified phone number. AcmeCloud recommends an authenticator app over SMS because SMS can be intercepted through SIM-swapping attacks. During setup, the account holder is shown a set of one-time backup recovery codes, which should be stored somewhere safe outside the account itself, since they are the fastest way to regain access if the MFA device is later lost or unavailable.

If an account holder loses access to their multi-factor authentication device and does not have their backup recovery codes saved, self-service recovery is not possible for security reasons. This situation requires contacting AcmeCloud support directly and completing an identity verification process, which may include confirming billing details, account creation date, and recent account activity. MFA cannot be disabled or bypassed based on an email request alone, and support staff cannot remove MFA on a live chat without verification, since doing so could allow an attacker to take over the account. Verification and MFA removal are handled manually by the security team and are not something documentation alone can resolve.

AcmeCloud subscriptions bill either monthly or annually, depending on the plan selected at signup or after a later plan change. Invoices are generated automatically on each renewal date and are available under Account Settings > Billing > Invoice History, where they can be viewed online or downloaded as a PDF. Invoices include the billing period covered, the plan name, the amount charged, and the payment method used. Invoice history is retained for the life of the account and does not expire. Account holders who need invoices reissued with different billing details, such as a company name or tax ID correction, should update their billing profile before the next renewal, since past invoices cannot be edited after generation.

Occasionally a customer may see what looks like two charges from AcmeCloud on their statement around the same date. In many cases one of these is a temporary authorization hold placed by the payment processor to verify the card is valid, rather than an actual charge, and it is automatically released within 5 to 7 business days without any action needed. If both charges post as completed transactions rather than holds, or if the duplicate remains after 7 business days, this cannot be confirmed or resolved from documentation alone. It requires looking up the specific account's billing history to determine whether an actual duplicate charge occurred, and if so, the billing team issues a refund for the erroneous charge once confirmed.

When a scheduled subscription payment fails on AcmeCloud, the system automatically retries the charge up to three times over the following 7 days, using the payment method on file. An email notification is sent after each failed attempt, along with a reminder to update the payment method if needed. If all three retries fail, the account is switched to a restricted mode: existing data remains accessible for export, but most features are disabled until payment succeeds. The account is not deleted or permanently canceled at this stage. Updating the payment method at any point, including after entering restricted mode, triggers an immediate new charge attempt rather than waiting for the next scheduled retry.

AcmeCloud's current refund policy allows refund requests within 14 days of a charge for annual subscription plans. Monthly plans are generally non-refundable, since they can be canceled at any time to stop future charges, except in cases of a confirmed billing error, such as being charged after a valid cancellation. All refund requests, whether for annual or monthly plans, go through manual review by the billing team rather than being issued automatically, and approved refunds are processed back to the original payment method within 5 to 10 business days. Refund eligibility outside these windows is evaluated case by case and is not guaranteed, so documentation alone cannot confirm whether a specific request will be approved.

Under AcmeCloud's previous refund policy, all subscription plans, monthly and annual, were eligible for a refund within 30 days of any charge, and eligible refunds were issued automatically without manual review once the request was submitted through the billing portal. This policy has since been replaced by a shorter, review-based refund window that distinguishes between monthly and annual plans. This older 30-day, no-review policy should not be used to answer current refund questions, since it no longer reflects how refund requests are evaluated or how quickly they are issued.

Payment disputes and chargebacks, where a customer contacts their bank or card issuer directly rather than AcmeCloud to reverse a charge, cannot be resolved through documentation or self-service. Once a chargeback is filed, AcmeCloud is notified by the payment processor and the disputed amount may be held or reversed while the case is investigated, which can take several weeks depending on the card network's process. Accounts with an open chargeback are typically placed in a restricted state until the dispute is resolved, since the funds are in question. Customers are encouraged to contact AcmeCloud billing support directly before filing a chargeback, as disputes filed with the bank instead of support often take longer to resolve and can temporarily affect account access.

An AcmeCloud subscription can be canceled at any time from Account Settings > Billing > Manage Subscription. Canceling stops future automatic renewals but does not immediately end access: the account holder retains full access to their current plan's features until the end of the billing period they already paid for. After that period ends, the account moves to the free tier if one exists for that account type, or becomes read-only, depending on the plan. Canceling does not automatically delete account data. There is no partial refund for the unused portion of a canceled billing period, aside from cases that qualify under the standard refund policy.

Previously, canceling an AcmeCloud subscription took effect immediately: as soon as cancellation was confirmed, the account lost access to paid features right away, even if part of the billing period had already been paid for, and no continued access was granted for the remainder of that period. This immediate-cancellation behavior has since been changed so that canceled accounts retain access until the end of the current paid billing period instead. This older behavior should not be used to describe what happens when a customer cancels today.

Upgrading an AcmeCloud subscription to a higher-tier plan takes effect immediately once confirmed in Account Settings > Billing > Manage Subscription. The account gains access to the new plan's features right away, without waiting for the next renewal date. The cost difference between the old and new plan is prorated based on the number of days remaining in the current billing cycle and charged to the payment method on file at the time of the upgrade. The next full renewal charge, after the upgrade, reflects the new plan's regular price. Upgrades can be made at any point during a billing cycle and are not limited to renewal dates.

AcmeCloud offers a 14-day free trial on eligible plans, giving full access to that plan's features without an upfront charge. A payment method is required to start a trial on most plans, though it is not charged during the trial itself. A reminder email is sent 3 days before the trial ends, letting the account holder know the trial will automatically convert into a paid subscription unless it is canceled beforehand from Account Settings > Billing. If the trial is canceled before it ends, no charge occurs. Only one free trial is available per account and per payment method; accounts that have already used a trial are not eligible for a second one on the same or a different plan.

API keys for an AcmeCloud account are created and managed under Developer Settings > API Keys. Each key is displayed in full only once, at the moment it is created, and is not retrievable afterward for security reasons; if it is lost, a new key must be generated. Keys should be stored securely, such as in a secrets manager, and never committed to source control or shared over unencrypted channels. Revoking a key from the Developer Settings page takes effect immediately and cannot be undone. Regenerating a key invalidates the previous one right away, so any application still using the old key will begin failing requests until it is updated with the new one.

Under the current AcmeCloud API usage policy, rate limits are tiered by plan: Standard-plan API keys are limited to 1,000 requests per minute, and Enterprise-plan keys are limited to 5,000 requests per minute. Requests exceeding the limit receive an HTTP 429 response along with a Retry-After header indicating how many seconds to wait before retrying. Rate limits are applied per API key, not per account, so an account with multiple keys has the limit enforced separately on each one. Sustained or repeated abuse of rate limits, such as intentionally sending bursts far beyond the limit, may result in temporary key suspension. Plan-level rate limit increases beyond the Enterprise tier are handled through a separate request to the sales team.

Previously, AcmeCloud enforced a single flat API rate limit of 100 requests per minute per key across all plans, with no distinction between Standard and Enterprise tiers. This flat limit has since been replaced by a tiered structure that gives higher limits to Enterprise-plan keys. This older flat 100-requests-per-minute figure should not be used to answer current questions about API rate limits, since it no longer reflects the limits actually enforced on Standard or Enterprise plans.

Account holders can export their AcmeCloud account data from Account Settings > Data > Export Data. An export includes account and profile information, activity logs, and any content stored under that account, available in CSV or JSON format depending on the data type. Generating an export can take up to 48 hours depending on the amount of data involved, and a download link is emailed to the account's verified email address once it is ready. For security, the download link expires 7 days after it is generated, after which a new export request must be submitted. Data exports do not include billing details such as full payment card numbers, since that information is held by the payment processor rather than AcmeCloud directly.

Deleting an AcmeCloud account is permanent but includes a 30-day grace period before the deletion is finalized. During those 30 days, logging back in with the same credentials reactivates the account and restores all data. After the 30-day grace period ends, all account data, including content, activity history, and billing records tied to the account, is permanently deleted and cannot be recovered by support or any other means. An active paid subscription must be canceled before an account can be deleted; deletion does not automatically cancel a subscription or stop future billing. Account deletion requests are submitted from Account Settings > Data > Delete Account and require re-entering the account password to confirm.
